utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom, especially those assisting us. Before we give an opportunity for the Defence to call its next witness, Madam Registrar, I think we first should call the case and then deal with the documents, first. Would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. We'd like first to deal with the documents that have been introduced by the witness that was examined yesterday. Could you assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1804, under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit D1805, map marked by Witness DP50; Exhibit P3764, black and white photograph -- photocopy of photo of M-48; P3765, black and white photocopy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Since there are no objections, all these documents are admitted into evidence, D1804, pseudonym sheet under seal. Ms. Pilipovic, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Your Honour, yes, I am ready for the next witness. With your leave, I'd like to raise an issue which may come up which is that one of the hearing on the 8th of January, and we'd just like to ask for the opinion or the position of the Chamber so that we can resolve this problem. We will have a problem regarding the arrival of witnesses on the 7th of January, which is Christmas Day. The Defence would like to have a schedule and a position of your Chamber, either today or the next day, and also we would like to then see how we are going to organise the witnesses for that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The suggestion of the Chamber was that you would, if possible, call a witness on the 8th of January who is not of the Orthodox religion. Since in other religions, Christmas Day is usually on the 25th of December. So, therefore, if you would have a witness who does not have his Christmas Day on the 7th of December, he could arrive on the 7th of December, and then we could continue on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has given it some thought, but we will not be able to confirm the arrival of another witness who doesn't celebrate this holiday for the reason that it is only after we finish this part of the case, that is mid-December, that we will or end of December that we will know which witness will arrive when, if we are talking about the hearings in January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has decided that it will respect the Orthodox holidays, but to the extent necessary. That means that we are losing two days in court and the Chamber fully accepts that, but a third day would not be acceptable in the eyes of the Chamber. So, therefore, if you say I cannot yet schedule, then perhaps you should schedule in a -- in such a way that you have to find someone on your list and then perhaps it will not be the preferred order to call this witness at that very moment, but that's then perhaps one of the perhaps the price you have to pay for the full respect the Chamber gives to the Christmas, the Orthodox Christmas. So I would very much like the Defence to find out whether a witness could be found that could be heard on the 8th, and, of course, it is -- the Chamber expects that it is someone who is not celebrating Christmas on the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in any case, we will think about this, but obviously I will be working on the 7th and I will be here. I will discuss this with my co-counsel whether we will be in a position to have a witness ready for the 8th. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber expects you to have a witness ready for the 8th. Then we also had the outstanding issue of maps on which the parties would inform the Chamber. Perhaps if that could be done at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. You yesterday stated the preference that the Defence and Prosecution discuss it first and see if there was any basis for agreement. I spoke to Madam Pilipovic yesterday afternoon and she wishes me to speak to Piletta-Zanin, to Mr. Piletta-Zanin and there will not be an opportunity -- there has not been an opportunity for that to happen because he is still on his way back to The Hague, as I understand it. So I have arranged a meeting this afternoon with Mr. Piletta-Zanin and Madam Pilipovic to inform them of what we have in mind and discuss it. So in those circumstances it would seem that perhaps tomorrow would be a more appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we will hear from you tomorrow. Then, Ms. Pilipovic, I understood that you are ready to call your next witness. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. I am informed that you would prefer to have a Bible with you when making this declaration. As you will see from the text of the declaration, it's neutral as far as the religion is concerned. If it would add something for you personally to have a Bible with you when making the declaration, nothing in the Rules opposes against it, but the text you'll have to pronounce should be the text we find in the Rules. That text will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I am just checking on whether this witness is already in the list of protective measures. Could you -- I have not yet mentioned his name. Let me just check on my list.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the submission dated 25th of November the Defence refers to the submissions from the 25th of September and 21st of October regarding the pseudonym and facial distortion asked for this witness, and in the submission of the 25th of November, the Defence also submitted a slightly enlarged summary regarding the protective measures sought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am just checking on whether we have a decision on the protective measures or not. No, we have not. The additional information you've given, would that create -- would that give rise to any objection from the Prosecution? If not, then the decision is now given orally that protective measures are effective in respect of you. And I was informed that they were, as a matter of fact, in effect when you entered this courtroom, so that was perhaps a bit too early, but we are on the safe side. So protective measures have been granted. Ms. Pilipovic -- and the protective measures are pseudonym, that is DP19, if I am well informed, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And facial distortion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. DP19, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I start asking you questions, I am going to hand you a document that you will look at, please. And if you can confirm whether the information contained on the sheet is correct, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: The information on the sheet is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind that always when we start the examination-in-chief we ask certain questions that could reveal his identity and in order to obtain a more substansive information, I wanted to ask for private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is confirmed on my screen that we are in open session. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, considering that you told us where you lived and you worked, in the course of the examination we will be speaking about the period from September 1992 until August 1994. In September, in the area where you lived, you lived and you worked there, can you tell us how were you engaged and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: In September, I lived and worked as I have explained earlier in the municipality of Hadzici, and I went about my business every day and worked and lived there. However, on the 8th of May sometime at about 12.00, 12.00 noon, as far as I can recall, the maintenance institute, all workers of other nationalities left that institute, Muslims and Croats, and only a part of the personnel remained to work there. We didn't know why that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, I am sorry, I have to interrupt you. What I asked you was whether in September 1992 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: In September 1992, I was on the line, I was on the first front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were on the first front line, can you please clarify. In what capacity and where were these first front lines? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I was there in the capacity of an ordinary soldier, a private. I was on the line at the foot of Mount Igman in the village of Kastici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that in 1992 you were on the line, perhaps I misunderstood, was it at the foot of Igman, below?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: At the foot of Mount Igman, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us when was this line established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: That line was established much earlier, much earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, when you say "much earlier" can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Immediately after the conflict broke out, that was sometime in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, can you tell us what was the ethnic composition of the municipality of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: The ethnic composition of the municipality of Hadzici of the urban part of the actual town, that was half and half, 50-50, considering the municipality of Hadzici is slightly larger and then it would include also the villages that surrounds it. That's where slightly the Muslim population was in majority, probably 74 to 75 per cent in respect of other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that the line was established much earlier, can you tell us how did it happen, how did it occur that these lines were established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: If I have understood your question, you are asking me about the beginning of the war itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. DP19.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, just a moment ago I perhaps -- I started to answer to you are question perhaps in a confused manner. But as I said a moment ago, on the 8th of May, the maintenance institute, all the nationalities except the Serb nationality workers, they all left. We didn't know what was happening. We didn't know what was going on. A number of people who remained there and to protect the institute, to continue to work, normally to carry out their duties, they experienced shooting on the institute itself, and I believe that is how the war started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, I am going to interrupt you. Are you telling us that there was a division that occurred along ethnic lines in the municipality of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, the division occurred much earlier, in 1992, immediately following the referendum, and the referendum was only answered by Muslims, as far as I know. Nobody else. And already the division occurred then. And following the February in 1992, because I was the head of the restaurant, I experienced that one of the workers said to me: "We have counted ourselves. We are not afraid of you." That was a cook who worked for me and his name was Hujic Rasid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, thank you. When you were talking about the lines, how were these lines established in relation to the municipality of Hadzici? I mean, what lines are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I am talking about demarcation lines, that is at the -- in one moment we just consolidated ourselves, we organised ourselves as a unit in terms of the institute and the Territorial Defence, which had to protect the institute as a factory, and obviously also civilian population which Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was already down there. So we tried to organise ourselves, the population which was living on the border areas so that we can -- so that we can be there. That's very near the institute, very near.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to speak a bit slower. Every word you say will be interpreted into a language we understand and the interpreters, with your speed, might have some problems. And we'd really like to hear what you tell us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you mentioned the establishment of the demarcation lines, between whom exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Between the Muslims who had left their houses a long time ago, who had left their villages. And on the other side, the Serbs who had remained in the city itself, and the civilian population, there families, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you told us that you worked in a technical and maintenance institute, that the citizens of Hadzici organised themselves into a Territorial Defence in order to protect the technical and maintenance institute. Can you tell us what the purpose of the technical and maintenance institute was? What sort of a work organisation was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Before the war broke out, the technical and maintenance institute was involved in all repairs -- in the repairs of all weapons of the former JNA, Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP19, in 1992, September 1993, August 1994, do you know whether the technical and maintenance institute functioned during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: In September 1992 and in 1994, the technical and maintenance institute remained where it was and continued to function. But it was for the Army of Republika Srpska that was subsequently established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, can you tell us at what capacity the technical and maintenance institute worked during that period, the period is 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: It worked at reduced capacity because perhaps 200 workers remained within the institute. We tried to repair the weapons that we had all the time and make them function properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is not an objection. I do not at this point know the relevance, but perhaps we could have the witness indicate the source of his knowledge about the capacity of a weapons maintenance unit in Hadzici, when he told us that he spent his time in that period on the front lines in a village elsewhere. So, perhaps just for the record we could know exactly what is the basis of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please clarify, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, can you tell us with regard to the answer you gave to my question, you stated that the institute worked at reduced capacity. Do you have direct knowledge of this or did someone tell you about this? If someone told you about this, could you be a little more precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Perhaps it is difficult for me to find my bearings in all of this because I am not well -- very well familiar with the legal terminology. I said that when the war broke out I was in the institute, that was on the 8th of May. I was there for a very short period of time. As I was a worker who dealt with logistics in the institute, I know how many people came to have meals there. And that is why I said that I knew at what capacity the technical and maintenance institute was working. But very quickly, very soon, I was transferred to the front line, as this was necessary, from the institute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my better understanding, when were you transferred to the front lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Four or five days later. I think it was the 12th or the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question now is -- that is still in May, as far as I understand. Now, the question is the basis of your knowledge on the reduced functioning of the institute on from September 1992 up until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand. What do you mean, what is the basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that you knew that there were less -- there was less capacity because you knew the number of people getting their meals. But when once you left approximately mid-May, how would you know on from that moment what the capacity of the institute was? Because you would not see the people getting their meals, isn't it? So there must have been another way of knowing it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I heard about this from people who would bring us food, who would bring food to the positions. And as I said earlier on, only about 200 employees remained in the technical and maintenance institute. I think that that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you heard from those people who brought you food in your positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, when you say that you were at the lines and positions, can you tell us how were you organised in terms of military establishment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: It was the size of a company. Was it the size of a company, is that what you are asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I am asking you about September 1992. In terms of establishment, were you a company and how many men were there in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: In September 1992, there were a number of men because from May until September the unit was brought up to strength as refugees came from other areas and to be more specific, Zenica. I don't remember the exact period. But in terms of establishment we had perhaps grown into a battalion, that was in September 1992. That's what the situation must have been then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you said that in September 1992 you were in a battalion. But can you tell us where the command of your battalion was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: In Zunovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, when you say in Zunovica, can you tell us what sort of feature this is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: This was a feature which was part of the former JNA, which belonged to the former JNA, an engineer unit, Karlo Batko, that was the full address. It was one of the military institutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, did you personally go to that facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, it is not just one facility. There are several facilities, depending on the needs of the JNA at the time. There were buildings, offices there, social canteens, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you said that the battalion command was located there, in those premises. Do you know, do you personally know whether there were any members of the former JNA there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "no," is this on the basis of your personal knowledge or is it something that you were told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: It is on the basis of my own personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you know exactly, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I know that at that time none of the active-duty officers was with us, apart from those from the reserve forces and these are men whom I knew, I would see them on a daily basis, and I cooperated with them, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, are you telling us that the JNA had withdrawn from that territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. The JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew and took everything it could with it. Certain things remained, I don't know how much. It wasn't something that interested me, but as early as May Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 1992, the JNA had left that area and taken everything with it, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you mentioned your position, your line, you said at the foot of Mount Igman. Can you tell us something about those demarcation lines which were in the area where you were located? Can you tell us what the positions of these demarcation lines were for both armies in that territory? Do you know anything about this? Could you provide us with further details about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, as an ordinary soldier, what could I know, apart from the fact that we dug trenches in order to protect our lives, to protect ourselves. I think that the enemy side did the same. And when I say "the enemy side," I mean the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, when you said that the urban part of the town of Hadzici, the urban part of the municipality of Hadzici had 50 per cent Muslims and 50 per cent Serbs, and you said that the rural parts had more Muslims. Did such a situation remain in the course of the war and did it change? When I say "in the course of the war," I mean from September 1992. So what was the ethnic composition in that area and what did the lines look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Most of the inhabitants of the town centre, they were mostly Serbian, and there were some Croats, perhaps they were civilians, whereas the Muslims had left earlier on. They pulled out with what they had left, those who could leave had left, children, women, elderly people and some livestock from certain villages had been taken away, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you mentioned the demarcation lines, can you tell us how far the demarcation lines were or what the distance was between the demarcation lines between the Serbs who had organised themselves in that area and the Muslims who were also in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Since we were down below at the periphery of the town, they were about 500 metres from us as the crow flies, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were down below, what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Towards the town itself, let's say Igman is far away. They were already there. We were in the village of Kastici, that's at the foot of Mount Igman. That's what I meant to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mount Igman and your positions in relation to Igman. Can you tell us in that area where your lines were and in the period that you were present there, September 1992, can you tell us whether there was any fighting in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: There was fighting all the time from May up until September. Up until the end of the year 1992, there was a large-scale fighting because they tried to break through our front lines every day and enter the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long you remained at that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Until the beginning of 1993, until February, which is when the Army of Republika Srpska had already organised itself and it was necessary to establish a military canteen so that the soldiers could be given food on a daily basis. As I was qualified for this in terms of my military occupational specialty, I was made responsible for the canteen, and I did that until the end of the war, from February until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, when you say that the Army of Republika Srpska was formed and that you were engaged elsewhere from February, can you tell us in the area of the municipality of Hadzici, which is a part of the town of Sarajevo, when were the military authorities established and the military functions of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, this was an ongoing process, from June to September 1992, and up until the end of 1993. As I said, units were brought up to strength every day as people arrived, refugees from other areas. So anyone fit for military service was engaged. I apologise, but at the moment it is difficult for me to be precise. I said in 1993 it was necessary to establish a military canteen and so that's the period that it concerns, from May up until that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you said that in September in terms of establishment you were in a battalion. And was that unit present throughout the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Don't hold it against me if I misunderstand your question occasionally. I think I have understood this now. Throughout that time it wasn't just the battalion there, but the units also grew and they developed, so an Igman Brigade was also formed, which later consisted of three battalions and even later of four. And I know this on the basis of my own experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know when the Igman Brigade was formed in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, I don't have that information, but I know that it was from June to September, to the end of the year, up until the end of the year, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, while you were at the line at the foot of Igman, you said that there was fighting. Can you tell us how you were armed and how the members of your company were armed? What weapons did you use and similarly, I'd like to ask you the same question for the BH Army. Can you tell us anything about this with regard to that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Our army, the Army of Republika Srpska had infantry weapons, automatic and semi-automatic rifles. And the other side also had infantry weapons, and they also had some large-calibre weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "large-calibre weapons," do you personally know the calibre concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know for certain that in the Pazarici Barracks, I don't know how to describe it, a unit of the artillery educational centre remained there, regiment with young cadets. I know this. I've got to go back --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, since we don't have much time, when you say that there was a regiment in Pazarici, when did you find out about what there was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I think it was the 19th or 20th of May because I happen to be at home then, and I went to the technical and maintenance institute to see the men from the logistics section. I spoke to the drivers, to Dobrica Micic and Zivko Tesic, who used two buses from the technical and maintenance institute to get the young cadets out, the young cadets who had been blocked there. And they said that in the barracks in Pazarici a lot of equipment had remained there, heavy weapons too. I don't know of what calibre, but I know that there were a lot of heavy weapons there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the Muslims fired from Mount Igman from large-calibre weapons. Can you tell us while you were at the line did you know what sort of weapons the Muslims were firing from in the direction of your lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: From field guns, from mortars. A Browning, I think that's a heavy weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you said that they used field guns, that they fired from field guns. Could you first of all tell us how far Mount Igman was from your positions? And I mean the positions of the BH Army, the positions from which they used their cannons, their field guns.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, 5 or 6 kilometres as the crow flies. They were on the other side of the -- of Mount Igman. Five or 6 kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they fired from field guns from the Igman mountain you told us how far away they were as the crow flies, can you tell us what they aimed at? Were you able to see what they were firing at when they fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't possible to see --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I know where counsel is going. Perhaps it can be rephrased because the way the question is phrased is really asking him to go into the minds of somebody 5 or 6 kilometres away. He asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he has answered the question by now, as you see it on your screen, that you couldn't see it. Yes. The question was whether the witness was able to see what they were firing at from a distance of 6 kilometres, that's 5 or 6 kilometres. That's a question that almost invites for speculation. If it would have been differently formulated, the risk of speculation would have been less. Please proceed and keep this in mind, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you told us that the Muslims used field guns from the area of Mount Igman. Did you personally see certain places which were fired at from guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw traces in the town itself. They shelled on a daily basis. Every day many shells fell in Hadzici, perhaps several hundred. When I returned home from the line in order to change my clothes, to pick up something, I can say that there were visible traces on the buildings, in the asphalt, in car parks. You could see the craters that had been caused by these shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, I think you said that mortars were also fired.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which positions and do you know this personally, from personal experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: From which positions we knew, what their positions were, and they constantly attacked from there. The attacks were carried out from Pazarici, villages of Gradac, Zovik, Lokve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, so that we have a clearer idea about the area that you are talking about, the Defence would like to show you a map, with the leave of the Chamber, where you could show us which area is it that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the copy of the map, C2, the document that the Defence has brought along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Madam Usher, could you please put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I have a look at it quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There are not many copies available, so...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll use this time to ask Mr. DP19 a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, when you are talking about these places, Pazarici, Gradac and so on, how far away are these villages from the centre of the Hadzici locality, from the urban centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: About 6 kilometers, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of the municipality is the village of Tarcin also located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: The village of Tarcin is slightly further off, a little bit further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any knowledge whether in 1992, 1993, 1994, there was an army there, BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pazarici, Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Muslim Army, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you have a map next to you, Mr. DP19, do you recognise this part of the section of the map that you have on your right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, I was not in a position to see this map, but I recognise -- I recognise the entire area. Could you perhaps show me how to show this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you could turn to your right ask tell me what you recognise on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Pazarici, Zovik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, with the pointer, please, can you show the area of Hadzici. Perhaps you could lift that part of the map so that you can have a better look.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Here it is. Of course, here it is. It's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this map, can you tell us about the lines of the Republika Srpska Army and the BH Army lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: The VRS lines, these are the -- in red, marked in red. And the Muslim Army lines are the other colour. I don't know whether it is green or blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, can you tell us whether here the positions where you were are visible? Can you locate it for us, this area where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Here it is. The Kastici, village of Kastici, that's where I was. There was an elevation point above Hadzici, Tinovo. Then next to the maintenance facility of Guncar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are talking about the elevation points, the dominating elevation points, are you saying that on the elevation point that was dominating, can you tell us which one it is that you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Tinovo, Guncar -- are you asking me about our elevation points?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am asking you about what were your dominating elevation points.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: The hill of Tinovo in Hadzici itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, bearing in mind that told us about the Republika Srpska dominating elevation points -- point, can you tell us or can you show us the position of the BH Army when we are speaking about the dominant positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: These points, as I have called them, the dominant points, they are lower than theirs. They always had higher points, Igman, Ormanj, all of them. They were even linked up all the way to Tarcin, to their villages. And all of that was higher up than we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that in this area, in this part of the town of Hadzici, it was in this part in relation to the Republika Srpska Army positions, the positions of the BH Army were dominant because they were on more elevated positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Because Hadzici is in a valley. These two elevation points I've mentioned earlier, they have no importance in relation to their positions because their positions were always higher. Hadzici was in a kind of hole. They were always on higher positions than we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you are telling us that in this area there was the Igman Brigade that was there, that's what you told us. Can you tell us if you know who was the commander of the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: That was Blagoje Kovacevic. I think his name -- his first name is Blagoje, but he was there for a short time. After that a man called Dunjic came and after Dunjic, there was Spasoje Cojic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us that in September you were in the battalion can you tell us who was the commander of the battalion, your battalion commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I think it was Petar Milosevic. I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period of time while you were military active person, you were on the line, did you receive certain orders? If you did, who did you receive them from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, the battalion commander was probably [Realtime transcript read in error "possibly"] giving orders to company commander, and then they gave orders to us. There was a strict order not to fire, not to open fire, not to fire on anything except respond in firing against firing. Save ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, for the transcript, what I heard is in the last answer is that the battalion commander was "probably giving orders," and not "possibly." May I just draw your attention that I heard something different. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, can you tell us whether you personally were given orders, did you hear orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes, I did, while I was in the positions, myself and all my fellow combatants from the platoon commanders, don't fire at random, save ammunition, only fire when it is necessary. Respond with firing if there is firing from the other side. And we stuck to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, on this map when you indicated the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and the BH Army, you told us that the Hadzici -- that Hadzici was in a valley, in a dip; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes. They were in a valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long was the front line of the Igman Brigade in relation to the Hadzici area? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of communication, whether you had communication with the rest of the city of Sarajevo during 1992, 1993, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Since Hadzici is located, as I said, in a valley and the border areas were held by the Muslim forces, Hadzici had one single exit. What I am saying is that they were completely encircled. The only exit point was towards Blazuj in order to communicate with the rest of the world, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, can you tell us personally, since you said that the technical institute or maintenance institute was working with a diminished capacity, you said that later on in the brigade there were several battalions. Can you tell us which ones were these battalions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: 1st Infantry Battalion, 2nd Infantry Battalion, and 3rd Battalion. Later on, as time went on, there was another one that was established. I don't know what it's name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you told us about the fighting that went on. Can you tell us about the intensity of the fighting? We are talking about September 1992 through August 1994. How was the intensity of the fighting? Can you perhaps elaborate on that a little? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: There was daily, daily shelling from the side of the Muslim Army of our positions, and even of the civilian population, of the urban part of town. For instance, attacks were so intense that -- so fierce, that on the 19th of April, specifically on 1993, at the building entering the house, my own son, my only son was killed entering his house, entering the house, including a friend of his called Srdjan Zuza. There was a lot of constant fighting and shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you told us that you had trenches. Can you tell us when did you dig the trenches in the area of your line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, immediately after the war broke out, when the line was established -- perhaps I am speaking too fast -- as soon as the demarcation lines was established, as the manpower arrived, as the manpower levels were increased, then the personnel were digging themselves in and trenches were dug. It didn't happen overnight. It was gradually done. I don't know how to explain it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you told us that the Muslims from their positions were firing with a Browning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which position was that that they held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I do know that. Just a moment. Here it is, from Gradac, from Pazarici, that's village of Lokve. But the Browning was firing from the position of so-called Suplja Stijena, it's a hollow rock position, and the Browning -- that is what our fellow combatants were saying, the soldiers were saying, that the Browning was there, Browning was firing all the time. It was firing on the town. And that is a 12.7 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, while the conflict was ongoing in the area of Hadzici, can you tell us was there ever a truce in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: In that area, there was some decisions that were reached in relation to truce, but it was simply a lie. It was never respected. Any truce was never respected, and I state this with certainty. They shelled us and fired on us day and night and this was just -- this was just formal agreements that never came to anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you informed about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I was informed in such a way that they shelled us, they fired on us all the time. And the night before we would find out from the media that there was truce or ceasefire signed, but there was nothing came of it. I felt this on my own skin. Every day there was firing and I had to protect myself in order not to suffer the fate of so many civilian victims, and as I said earlier, of my only son, who was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, one other question and then the examination-in-chief will be over. When you were telling us about the area of Pazarici and Tarcin, did you have personal knowledge whether in these areas, were there camps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. There were, there were two camps. One was in Krupa, that is next to Pazarici, right next to Pazarici. Krupa. I don't know where Krupa is marked here on this map. And, of course, the infamous silo in Tarcin, of course, I know that. Because the people who escaped, some, as it happened, managed to escape from working up there from the digging of trenches. Some people managed to save themselves, but people know about these two camps. Practically the whole world knows about it, close who are interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has finished the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President, I don't know if it would be inconvenient to the court if we could take a break now and return for the usual period. I suspect that based on what I'm thinking, we may well be able to expedite proceedings quite significantly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then adjourn until five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, you'll be now examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- were, sir, on the line in the area of Kastici, yours was an infantry company? Now you nodded. Could you express --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good. Did the battalion that that company was a part of have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I don't understand. 1st Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Who was the commander of that battalion while you were serving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I don't know. Because I was up on the line, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you indicated that the brigade commander for a short time was a man by the name Blagoje Kovacevic. Do you know when his tenure of as commander of that brigade ended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: He was the commander for a very very short time, only a couple of months. And then a man called Dunjic came after him, but the period, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Dunjic who came after him, would he have come there in about October, about October 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I really don't know. Perhaps that was the time. But in any case, he arrived after Blagoje who was commander for a very short time. I don't know. I had the opportunity to see him in the street, we met in the street. But I really don't know about the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know who succeeded Dunjic or may I just put it to you: Can you recall if a Spasoje Cojic succeeded Dunjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Spasoje Cojic, I know him. He came in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- very well, go on, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he came then as brigade commander, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an artillery battalion or unit in the Igman Brigade, that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Considering that in 1993, since February of that year, I was -- my combat disposition was in the rear. There was a mechanised armoured company that was established. I know this from the information because Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this was information was in connection of the issuing of food, preparation of food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about an artillery battalion or artillery unit, a unit with heavy guns in the brigade, do you know of one being established or being existent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes. After that company, afterwards became a battalion, mechanised armoured battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You indicated some of the areas from which attacks came while you were on the front. Were these areas to the south and east -- I am sorry, withdrawn. Were the areas that you speak of in respect to this fighting, were they to the south and west of your positions near the village of Kastici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I have not much knowledge of geography. I said these were elevations. As I said earlier, these were slopes of Mount Igman that take you to the village of Lokve, and then they go down to Pazarici, then the road goes down to Pazarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't you agree with me that you -- you are saying, therefore, that you are not able to say whether these areas were to the south, south-west and west of your positions at the village that you were at? You are not able to help us on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were other lines, were there not, which encircled the city of Sarajevo itself; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: There were other lines, but I am only speaking about the area of the town of Sarajevo in the municipality of Hadzici where I was. Because Sarajevo includes Ilidza and Vogosca, et cetera, but I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So I take it you would not be able to assist us in respect of -- withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have nothing further, really, on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there any need to re-examine the witness, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has a question for you. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, if you please, if it is possible, could you tell me about a certain detail. You answered a question about the establishment of confrontation lines. You said, and I am quoting you in English [In English] "The Muslims who had left their houses a long time ago who had left these villages." [Interpretation] End of quote. What I'd like you to tell me: They left their houses, why was that and when was that, could you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I can tell you. They left, and I don't know why at that time, but then later on we all found out and felt it on our own skin. I think I explained that. They took their elderly, their young children with them, even cattle. That they were preparing themselves for something. This became obvious afterwards. But entering into their villages, for instance the village of Dupovci [Realtime transcript read in error "Dobravici"] which is practically right next to the technical institute that I mentioned, we found houses that were connected with communication trenches and trenches which gives me a right, I think, to believe that they were preparing for war. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Preparing for war by withdrawing from the locations, from the villages, and even from the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes. I explained that. Upon entering this village later on, it was obvious, we could see the traces. We could see the holes for weapons, trenches. What else could it have been than preparation for a conflict? JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But didn't they have even a theoretical interest to stay because they were there, they were prepared, they had their trenches, they had their supplies. Having prepared all this, and then leaving without any obvious reason, don't you think that there is no exact reason why they left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I don't know what their objectives were, their reasons, their purposes. I was an ordinary private, an ordinary soldier. I worked for the quartermasters. Their reasons became apparent later on. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So what you can confirm, however, is that they had left and they left before May 1992, in April? Can you perhaps give us the time frame a little more precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: April, May 1992. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, I have one question for you as well. You told us that you could see the traces on the buildings of shelling, shelling the village of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you identify exactly where the shells came from? Could you see the positions from where the shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: You couldn't see the positions, but the shells came from the direction of Mount Igman because that's where they probably had heavy weapons. And the buildings, well, this was in the very centre of the town. In part, the buildings faced Mount Igman and in part they faced in another direction. There are still traces on these buildings to this very day and so now they are making attempts to repair what was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so these are conclusions on the character and the place of the damage done to the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Yes. And traces can be seen, there are the remainders of the weapons used, whether they were shells or I don't know what else they had, whether they were mortar shells or something else. My building was one such building too, the one in which I lived. I wouldn't like to speak about that terrible night for me again. That was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Mr. DP19, you've come a far way -- yes. Judge Nieto-Navia has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I am sorry, but regarding your answer to Judge El Mahdi, did I understand you well when you said that the Muslims left Hadzici and went to Dobravici and, there I mean in Dobravici, they built trenches, connecting trenches and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: I never mentioned Dobravici, as far as I can remember. The village of Dupovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Let me check. Page 33, line 6, it says "but entering into their villages, for instance, the village of Dobravici." Maybe it is a wrong transcription, but the question is: When you were referring to connecting trenches and so on, you were referring to another town, not to Hadzici. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: That village is a kilometre away. It is the suburbs of Hadzici itself. It is connected or perhaps it is 100 metres closer than the technical and maintenance institute. I know it very well. Because I lived there from 1964.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: My question is, you mentioned a place or a town where the Muslims built, you said, communication trenches and trenches. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Dupovci, the village which is right next to the technical and maintenance institute. And when I said we entered there, it was in order to get wood because winter was approaching and that is when we saw with what I mentioned a minute ago. The trenches and communicating trenches, and there was also food and cans of food in the basement. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions, or are there any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the forced deportation of any ethnic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. group in the villages surrounding Hadzici or that area? What is sometimes termed as "ethnic cleansing."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: That never happened. I can say that for sure, not while I was there in that area, and I was there throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when you went into some of the villages, the Muslim villages, they were empty. Am I correct in understanding that you did not know why they were empty of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP19
utterances.text: Well, we didn't know either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP19, this concludes your testimony in this court. I know that you've come a far way to The Hague. You've testified, you've answered questions of both parties and of the Bench, and of course you are testifying about a period in your life which also left its traces, its painful traces in your personal life and your family life. The Tribunal thanks you very much for coming to The Hague, for testifying, and I wish you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please guide us through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1806 under seal, pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is admitted under seal. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first look at -- that would be Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would be --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DP18, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check on our decision on protective measures. I haven't brought mine because it is on its way to be copied. Yes, protective measures have been granted in respect of the witness. Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, because that's how we will call you, we'll call you DP18 because protective measures have been granted in respect of you, that means your face cannot be seen and we will not use your name. Mr. DP18, before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration will be handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. You'll first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Would you like us to go in closed session perhaps to start with, perhaps after the pseudonym sheet?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Madam Usher, could you please assist Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. DP18.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, could you have a look at the piece of paper in front of you and could you tell us whether the information on the sheet of paper is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the next few questions we will turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we are in open session, you may please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, you told us that you worked up until the 20th of April 1992 up until the first attack on Ilidza. Before I ask you about the area in which you lived, can you tell us whether you know anything personally about the attack carried out against Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Not much, because I couldn't go to work --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who organised that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The Muslim forces from the direction of Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, the entire world saw that. There is such a thing as television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, Defence counsel will ask you some questions and could you tell us about the period which begins in September 1992 and goes on until August 1994. So this is the period during which you were in Hadzici. Tell us, in September 1992, were you engaged in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what capacity you were engaged in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, the armoured unit hadn't been established at that point. I was on a hill behind Hadzici. I was manning a weapon that was in fact defending our front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you served in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your military occupational specialty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I was an orderly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that in September you were at the defence line in Hadzici, can you tell us when these lines were established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, those lines were established around the end of May, maybe it was the end of May or mid-May, perhaps, something like that, after the last attacks carried out by the Muslim forces to take Hadzici and the technical and maintenance institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that until -- when you say that those lines were established in May after the Muslim attack, can you tell us how you were organised at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, the only organised unit was the technical and maintenance institute which was part of the JNA. Everything else was purely spontaneous. Because the first attack was carried out against the technical and maintenance institute which managed to defend itself on the 8th of May and everything else was organised on a voluntary basis. There were people who were practically defending their own houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that in September 1992 you were positioned and at a line that were established in May 1992? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. We could repeat that to avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute as to when approximately the lines were established prior to the indictment period? We hear a lot of evidence on that which seems to...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could respond to that. The evidence is that there was some movement in the confrontation lines between May and September, and that with a few exceptions which have been the subject of evidence such as Otes, they remain relatively steady thereafter. So if it assists, the Prosecution says there is no relevance in the position of the confrontation lines with precision before September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am not talking about precision. I am not talking about whether it was on the 15th or the 16th or the 17th. But in But in general terms, I think we hear a lot of evidence which comes down approximately, not always, but usually to the same, that people were defending themselves, that lines were established, and that it was for a great deal, spontaneous action. I mean, we heard that from many many many witnesses. Is there any need, unless there is a specific issue, of course, there is no problem if lines were changed to go over that again. Ms. Pilipovic, I am asking you because that takes approximately 5 to 10 minutes from each witness and I wondered whether we can -- of course, whether you could agree on it, that would be the best way of solving it. But I do not see such contradiction and since it is not one of the central issues in this case --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But I would just like my colleague to affirm that the line was established spontaneously, that the demarcation line was established spontaneously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not agree with that, Mr. President. We have heard evidence from Robert Donia as to the background as to the establishment of the lines, but in response your specific question, I don't believe there is any dispute, that the lines were established well before September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say the time when the lines were established is not very much in dispute, but whether it was spontaneous action, that is a different matter. Could you please keep that in mind for the future witnesses as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, in September 1992 you said that you were engaged in the military, you were in a company. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many men there were in the company in 1992, in September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, very few. I think there were between 20 and 30 men in that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were between 20 and 30 men in your company. In the area of the municipality of Hadzici, were there any large formations, and within which large formation did your company exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Within the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that it was part of the 1st Battalion, can you tell us how many men there were in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, up to about 600 men, I think. I don't know the exact number, but I think there were about 600 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were in a company. Can you tell us what kind of weapons your company had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Up until the end of 1992 it was a kind of armoured company and the weapons it had, well, I think it had two or three tanks, a Praga, a self-propelled rocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that your company had one self-propelled rocket, two or three rockets and a Praga, can you tell us what a Praga is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, a Prag, a P-R-A-G is a mobile weapon it had two barrels which the calibre is about 30 millimeters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, as a member of a company, which was part of a battalion, can you tell us who the battalion commander was, do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, before the witness answers the question, one of the previous answers in English reads that the company had two or three tanks, a Praga and a self-propelled rocket. And in your next question you say that when you say that your company had one self-propelled rocket, two or three rockets and a Praga. When you were talking about, Mr. DP18, two or three pieces of weaponry, did you refer to a tank or to rockets, two tanks or two rockets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tanks. A tank.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, my question was whether you could tell us who the battalion commander was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning I think it was Milosevic, but I've forgotten his first name. But I think that it was Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you tell us whether you personally know what greater formation did your battalion belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, I think until the end of September it was, it was at that time that they started establishing the Igman Brigade. Up until then, we existed as an armoured company within the 1st Battalion in Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the Igman Brigade" can you tell us how many smaller formations there were within the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many battalions there were in the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, I think there were about four battalions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were part of an armoured mechanised battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, first of all, it was an armoured mechanised company, and then when we had the brigade, they formed an armoured mechanised battalion, that was later on in September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the front line of your battalion was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which area that concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, that's the area that is behind the town, behind Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the positions of your battalion, can you tell us how far away were the lines or were there front lines of the BH Army in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, that was just above Hadzici. There was the -- a line going from Ormanj, Gaja, Borak, Gradelj and Igman and there was elevation point above Stupnik just above Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the positions of your battalion, where you were, can you tell us how far away were the positions of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: From my positions?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: A maximum up to 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you tell us in the period from September 1992 until August 1994, which weapons did your mechanised armoured battalion have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: We had about four or five tanks when we were established. We had a self-propelled gun. It had a Praga.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer, because the interpreters could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. It was B-R-D-M, it is an armoured vehicle, a Russian production. It is not caterpillars, but it's on wheels. B-R-D-M.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, and we are still speaking about the period September 1992 until August 1994, do you have personal knowledge whether in this area there was fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Throughout 1992 there were attempts of the Muslim forces to take over the municipality of Hadzici, that is the town of Hadzici itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there were attempts, can you tell us that fighting went on as well, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, until the end of 1992, nonstop, practically on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you have personal knowledge, what kind of weapons did the BH Army have in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Apart from infantry weapons, they also had mortars, that mortars were firing from the direction of Ormanj, Pazarici, Tarcin, and they also had heavier artillery which fired on Hadzici from Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they had heavy artillery, can you be a little more precise? What exactly did they have from heavy artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: These were field guns from 105 millimeters to 130 millimeters and they had remained at the Pazarici Barracks, after the Yugoslav Army withdrew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, when you were telling us about your battalion and when you were talking about the fighting, can you tell us what was the weapon that was issued to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I was a crew member on Praga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the daily fighting -- when you say fighting occurred on a daily basis, what weapons did you use to defend yourselves from the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: My battalion was only to give support to the first front lines because we were behind the front, some 1 and a half thousand to 2.000 metres. We would only be active if our infantry was at risk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit the first line, the front line of the infantry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Very rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the way that you communicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Via radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
