utterances.text: When you say that you took part -- that you were to give support when the infantry was at risk, can you tell us who issued orders to you, who gave you orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The battalion commander himself, when there was a request from the men who were on the first front line who were directly at risk from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you in these situations when you fired, did you have military targets that you fired on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: These were only military targets that we fired on, bunkers, trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far away were the bunkers and the trenches in relation to your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Infantry positions or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you know the infantry positions, then you can tell us first about the infantry positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you in some places it was even 100 metres, maximum it was 500 metres up to the trenches, 100 to 500 metres, depending on which part we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, when you are speaking about the lines, demarcation lines, speaking from a military strategic point of view, if you know, what were the positions of your battalion in relation to the BH Army forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The Muslim forces held all dominant elevation points above Hadzici, apart from the Tinovo elevation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the BH Army lines were established on those dominant points, elevation points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Immediately after the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, if the Defence shows you a map, would you be able to look at this map and mark on it, as you say, the military targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military targets, that were your targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, Ms. Pilipovic, that there will be no marking on this map, one of the few we have, but it can be put on the ELMO, and we will try to describe as precisely as possible. But let's keep the markers away from this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I can't see it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can turn to your right, it might be easier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this map can you point to the positions that you told us where the dominant points or dominant military points as you called them, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: This is the map which was practically until the end of the war, but before 1993, I can show you what it's like. Are you interested in what happened before 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the period both about 1993 and 1994, please, if you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The hill of Stupnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are pointing to the hill of Stupnik, what are you saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: They used infantry weapons and 60-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: This went on until July 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, for the transcript, the witness points to a position south-east from Hadzici, approximately in the middle between the village as indicated on the map and the red dotted line south-east of it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, are you saying that the line, the demarcation line between the two armies in that period that you are speaking about, 1993, it was different to what we can see on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that there was a shifting of the lines, a change in this period from 1993 until 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you pointed to this important strategic elevation point, do you know from which weapons BH Army members fired from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: They used infantry weapons, Browning gun 12.7 millimeters, and mortars. This was elevation point just above Hadzici. I don't know whether there was even one kilometre of distance as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this map, can you mark, can you point to other important strategic points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Elevation point Grada which was just above the barracks Zunovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are speaking about the Grada elevation point, can you tell us from this elevation point --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: A Browning gun, 12.7 millimetre was firing from this elevation point. It was firing from the -- at the point from the entrance to the barracks in Zunovica up to the 27th of July Street in the settlement, in the locality itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we are speaking about the Zunovica Barracks, this facility, during the conflict --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we move to the barracks, we first have to describe where the witness pointed at when he was speaking about Grada elevation point. That is south of the village of Hadzici where the both red and green confrontation lines in an angle of approximately 90 degrees change from north-south to east-west. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, my question was the barracks at Zunovica, can you tell us in 1992 who used the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Beginning or end of that year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you know you can tell us for chronology's sake.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, up to the 12th of May, something like that, that was the Yugoslav Army, until it withdrew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after it withdrew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: After it withdrew, the locals, the reservists, they remained at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether there were weapons there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: There were -- the JNA or the Yugoslav Army took away the weapons from 1991. Most of the weapons were withdrawn with the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information whether any weapons were left there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know because I wasn't there. I can't tell you if there was anything left. Most probably there were weapons left there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were speaking about the Grada elevation point, on this map, would you be able to point to some other elevation points if there were any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: There was the elevation point of Borak which the tank T34 was active, and from Gaja where there was the 20 millimetre anti-aircraft gun with two barrels, that was active from Gaja elevation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are speaking about the tank, Witness, and the positions from which the BH Army was active, can you tell us whether you personally saw this tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, it was not just one tank, there were two. Because when we destroyed the first one, the second one arrived and the second one was destroyed by the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us there was the first one and you said the second one was also destroyed at the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first tank, what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, I think it was by the end of 1992 that it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were telling us about the anti-aircraft gun, rocket launcher --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: No, no. This was the 20-millimetre anti-aircraft field gun with two barrels --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the range of that weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I think up to 3.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the BH Army fired from these tanks and from the anti-aircraft gun, can you tell us what were the targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, the targets were on our heavy weapons, the Praga, the tank, the self-propelled gun, those were the targets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have personal knowledge during the fighting whether on your side some weapons were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, on several occasions there were hits, but there was nothing --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, with you speaking about an elevation point, can you please tell us what was the elevation point from which the Muslims were active with the tank and the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: That was elevation point Borak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Elevation point Borak. Your Honour, just for the transcript, we have to explain that the witness for the elevation point Borak, he is pointing on the map between the green and the red line and the point is located above flag with number "1" on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you see on this map whether on the Borak elevation point there is a number, perhaps it will be easier to identify it then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: No, it just says "Borak" here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it is difficult to see from our screen, but where you say a flag with a number "1," would that be number 1 or a number 4? We have some doubt. You might be right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is closest and he says it's one, and having zoomed in, it comes closer to number "1" than to number" 4."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP, do you have personal knowledge or what is the range of the weapons that you are speaking about from the elevation point Borak of the anti-aircraft gun and of the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The tank is a weapon that shoots, fires directly, I think up to 18 to 20.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know personally whether the BH Army had field guns in certain positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I said that they had field guns on Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a field gun -- what the range of a field gun is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, they had so-called Sultan field gun, which I think it was 120 millimetre calibre, and it had a range up to 30.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in relation to your positions, how far away were the positions of the BH Army when they were firing the field guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Six to 7.000 metres, maximum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what targets they targeted in the municipality of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Most they targeted the technical maintenance institute --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us on the map whether it is possible to see the technical maintenance institute on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Approximately here, between Grivici and Kucice that's where the institute was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness pointed to the position of the technical maintenance institute of Hadzici which is located between the word "Grivici" on the left-hand side and on the right-hand side the word "Hadzici." Between these two words in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, you pointed to the Borak elevation point from which BH Army was firing. You said that there was also Igman. You indicated the military target for the Igman field guns was. Can you tell about more military targets in the municipality of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, the shells fell throughout the municipality of Hadzici, throughout the area that was inhabited, because that was the area that was targeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, next to the point Borak from which BH Army members were firing, on the front line, do you know whether there were other firing positions from which BH Army members were firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: We have Ormanj, that was the quarry, and from the heavy weapons, there they had the Bofors, 40-millimetre field gun, they also had a Browning gun, 12.7 millimetre. That was above the village of Dupovci, I think that's elevation 711, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness is indicating below the word "Dupovci" which is between the red and the blue line, and he is indicating the 716 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure whether it was 716 or 711. Nothing is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was from these positions that the BH Army was firing --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: With a Bofors 40-millimetre field gun and with a Browning 12.7-millimetre gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. DP18, you are speaking the same language. Could you please make a pause before you answer the question. If there is text on your screen which is not there at this very moment, you better wait until this text stops moving, so just make a short break. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP18, when we were speak about the fighting, you said that it was on a daily basis. In the period from 1992, 1993, through to 1994, what was the intensity of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, could you just repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The intensity of the fighting in the period from 1992, 1993, through to 1994.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, from September until the end of the year, the attacks were daily, and the shelling of our positions with their heavy artillery, and this occurred also on a daily basis. But the most -- the greatest attack in 1992 was on the 12th of December -- on the 19th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 19th of December when our positions were even fired on with rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are speaking about rocket launchers, do you personally have knowledge from which positions they were firing with rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: They were firing approximately from the direction of the village of Lokve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this map would you be able to indicate for us the village of Lokve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness is indicating on the map a point where we have a symbol, a flag with number "1" and below this flag there is a name place, place name called "Lokve." And the witness is indicating this as being the firing position of a multiple rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the actual weapon that was used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: That was the multiple rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are telling us that it was from this position in December of 1992 that this weapon was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge whether in the period of 1993, 1994, whether the positions from which this weapon was used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: After December of 1992, they didn't use rocket launchers from this side, because on that date, 19th of December, there was a frontal attack from Ormanj, from the hill Ormanj, all the way to Blazuj, they attacked our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the intensity of the fighting. Can you tell us whether in part of the town of Hadzici buildings were damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, of course. This can still be seen today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what sort of damage was caused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Damage was caused by mortars, Brownings firing from the quarry, artillery shells fired from Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, you have mentioned the firing positions, you have indicated the firing positions of the BH Army. Can you tell us whether there were any other firing positions from which they fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes. On the Koscan hill had a firing position there. They fired from the Koscan hill, they used mortars from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you just move the map a little to the right, please, so that we can point to the place. What was the name of the place you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Koscan.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness pointed above the black dotted line above the word Koscan. He pointed to a position from which the BH Army used mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is west from Hadzici. It's the other side of confrontation lines seen from Hadzici. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, you mentioned mortars. Is this on the basis of your own experience, of your own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the shell fins, when a shell explodes, the fin of a mortar shell remains intact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of personally seeing what the calibre was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the calibre was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: 82 millimetre and 120 millimetre, that was the calibre used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise -- you said 82 millimetres and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 120. Mr. DP18, in addition to the point that you have indicated, do you know whether there were any other firing positions from which the members of the BH Army were active in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The Ormanj hill, all these dominant positions around here were in their hands, from Koscan towards Dupovci and Hadzici. This line here, this belt here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness pointed to an area behind the blue line as far as the word "Pazarici" and said that this area was an area where the BH Army had position said from which it was active.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the witness pointed in approximately half a circle starting with Pazarici going up north following approximately the banded confrontation line on the western side. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you tell us about the position of Igman in relation to the town of Sarajevo? What was the position since you lived there, can you tell us anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: That was the part that was above the Sarajevsko Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, while you were engaged in the military in your battalion, can you tell us who the battalion commander was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Mr. Stajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was the company commander, or already it was a battalion and in the beginning it was a company. Can you tell us who gave you orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: From -- my commander did, Mr. Stajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the nature of these orders was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, we were told that we should only open fire when the lives of our men at the front lines were in danger. And we were told to save as much ammunition as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you tell us for the period of 1992, do you know whether there was a truce during that period and if there was, how often were there truces and how often were they made public?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: As far as I know in 1992 there were no truces at all. And in 1993 there were some, but they weren't respected much by the Muslim side because they would often fire from mortars at our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that the truces were not respected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they lasted, and if so, for how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I'd say 20 days, a month at the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When these truces were in force, can you tell us whether there was no fighting at the time or was the situation different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, there wasn't any fighting. There was shelling, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned shelling, but could you be a little more precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, shells fell on the technical and maintenance institute and in the very centre of the town, but not so many on our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say in the very centre of the town, can you tell us whether there were any military targets in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: No, not in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far were the lines? How far were the front lines of the Republika Srpska Army from the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, between 500 and up to 2.000 metres, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, can you tell us whether the technical and maintenance institute functioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "yes," do you have direct knowledge of this or is this something that someone told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, it was a military institution which worked for the needs of the army. It repaired artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, bearing in mind the fact that you have explained where the positions were, where the firing positions of the BH Army were, can you tell us where the military strategic positions of the BH Army were in relation to the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, since their positions were on the dominant elevations surrounding the town, we were in an inferior position in comparison to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, you mentioned the intensity of the fighting and the damage inflicted on the buildings. Can you tell us whether you personally saw where the most damage was done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, it was in the centre, that's the part that was most damaged, around the square, and the Zunovica neighbourhood, or rather the 27th of July Street and around the market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Zunovica" are you talking about the area where the Zunovica Barracks was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, the Zunovica Barracks was in the area behind the neighbourhood of Zunovica. It's name was Zunovica, but the neighbourhood of Zunovica was before the fishpond in Hadzici, and before the entrance into the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you use a felt tip to -- can you use the pointer to indicate that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: That's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to the Zunovica neighbourhood and said that this neighbourhood was the neighbourhood that was most damaged. It is next to the word, it says "Zunovica."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I see that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is next to number "1PP" on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you tell us what number "1PP" means, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. Only if it is to be brought in connection with the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you know who the commander of the Igman Brigade was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the time of its formation, do you know when the Igman Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: As far as I can remember it was towards the end of September. I think Kovacevic was the first commander. And afterwards it was Dunjic, and after Dunjic, Cojic, and finally I think that it was Petricevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you tell us whether you know whether the command post of the Igman Brigade was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: In the Blazuj Barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can that place be identified on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness pointed to the command post of the Igman Brigade which was in the Blazuj Barracks. He pointed to an area between the word "Igman Infantry Brigade" on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since you told us that there were several battalions in the Igman Brigade, do you know where the command posts of the battalions were located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: The 1st Infantry Battalion had its command post in the Zunovica Barracks itself, that's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to the command post of the first infantry battalion below the word "Zunovica" to the south.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd Battalion was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, just south of the village of Hadzici where he earlier for the Igman Brigade headquarters, he was pointing to a -- just left of where it reads "Blazuj" as far as I can see on the map, which is a village east from Hadzici. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, beneath the word "Zunovica" you pointed to the command post of the 1st Infantry Battalion in the barracks of Zunovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the sake of the transcript, I think that we said that it was to the south of the word "Zunovica" next to the word "the 1st Infantry Battalion" that's where the barracks is located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you could find a suitable moment for a break, and when you are referring to words, they usually appear as abbreviations in Cyrillic on the map. Would this be a suitable moment for a break? We will then adjourn until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a bit difficult without the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree. Yes, you would like to the raise --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I want to take this opportunity to say that this since this morning the Defence has not had a transcript in spite of the fact that the technical services intervened on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean no transcript on your laptop computer. Yes. I saw a technician coming in and finally no solution has been found. Then we will ask again whether someone will assist you, because the system as such seems to function well, but not at this very moment, for the Defence. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, before the break you showed us an area, you pointed to an area in response to my question concerning the command post of the battalions. Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to these places on the map and tell us what these places are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I first of all pointed to the command post of the brigade in Blazuj, the command of the 1st Battalion in the Zunovica Barracks. The command of the 2nd battalion in the village of Drozgometva --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. For the sake of the transcript, could you repeat the command post of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Drozgometva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this symbol means? Can you read out what it means in those black letters in the semi-circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: This isn't clear to me. I think the first letter is P.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anti-armour --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: No, it was an infantry battalion in Drozgometva, and it's number 2 here or it's a P. I can't make it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I say it is an anti-armoured attachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Anti-armoured attachment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the sake of the transcript, the witness has pointed to the command post of the 2nd Infantry Battalion in the black semi-circle where we can see the word Drozgometva.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Drozgometva, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above the word Hadzici, that would indicate the north-west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, can you point to the locations of the other command posts of the other battalions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I know the command post of my battalion, the armoured mechanised one, in the barracks Usivak, the Usivak barracks

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to the command post of the anti-armoured --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the armoured mechanised battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The armoured mechanised battalion in the area between the word -- the Igman Infantry Brigade and beneath the word "the 1st Infantry Battalion" 1PB means the 1st Infantry Battalion above the word "Igrava Brdo" [phoen] is the infantry brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said the Usivak barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP18.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, my colleague will ask a few more questions and then we will finish with our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would object on the grounds that I don't believe that Mr. Piletta-Zanin was present when the witness's testimony began, number one; and number two, in light of the fact that he has expressed problems with their LiveNote system, it would seem to me impossible that he could have reviewed the transcript during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I take note of that, of the fact that the Prosecution can see that we have been handicapped in these proceedings because we don't have our transcript. So I will respect a fair decision, but I would like to point out that this isn't the first time that we have had problems with the transcripts, whereas others do not have these problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I wanted to apologise, but my late -- my plane was very late this morning and in addition this isn't cross-examination, it is the examination-in-chief, and I have had the opportunity work with this witness personally. So I don't see how the fact that I wasn't able to see something which was not my fault, this was a technical problem, I don't see why this should be a problem for me to address certain issues which I wanted to address in the course of the examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, although it would have been the normal course, I would say, that Ms. Pilipovic would finish, the Chamber will allow you to further examine the witness, but under a condition, which will very very very strictly be observed, that wherever it appears that you are repetitious in your questioning or that your ask questions to the witness of which if you would have known the transcript, that you should not have asked it, then we will change it. You may instruct Ms. Pilipovic if you want to -- the Chamber noted that your objecting when that happened in cross-examination, this examination-in-chief, that is a bit different, so we will keep to that -- keep to this condition very strictly. And if the suggestion was in your words that your laptop suffers more than other laptops, I can tell you that my laptop failed to function many many times. Apart from that, I also can inform you that it is not possible to fix your laptop. It can be done, but parts have to be taken out and that could not be done during the course of the examination of the witness. If you need any assistance in that respect, if you would like to search for anything, I'll be glad to assist you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I work on the basis of memory for the most part, Mr. President. But we will see. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin: Witness, good day. You mentioned what we call multiple rocket launchers. VBR. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to know whether you had any kind of precise information about these weapons? And I don't mean where they were located, but I am referring to their nature, the type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, it's a weapon which is lethal. It depends on how many barrels it has, whether 12 or 32. So it can fire between 12 and 32 rockets at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The weapon that you have mentioned, and I am still referring to the multiple rocket launcher, what kind of a VBR was it? Was it a weapon that had many tubes? What do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: According to the information we received from the people who fled from Cine [phoen] and Pazarici, they said that they had 12 tubes and that they were of Chinese production, these multiple rocket launchers had 12 tubes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as you know did the Yugoslav Army usually have such VBRs, such multiple rocket launchers which were of Chinese production as part of its arsenal?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is a leading question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can put that question differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you have had any experience of this, do you know what kind of multiple rocket launchers, what kind of VBRs the former JNA had as part of its equipment? Do you know the answer to this question; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: All I saw was what I saw on television, but as far as the type of weapons are concerned, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, to return to more technical matters, you told us about the kind of multiple rocket launcher concerned, you said it was of Chinese production. Do you know what its range was? Did it have a long range, a short range, a longer or shorter range than weapons that were produced in Yugoslavia, and I am referring to the same type of weapon, VBRs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I think it was between 7 to 14.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, from the place where you knew that this VBR or these VBRs were located, what was the zone that was the end of the range of this weapon in relation to the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I would like to elaborate upon that in the absence of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, could you just -- could I ask you to escort the witness out of the courtroom for just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are attempting to locate the precise spot in the transcript, but my recollection is that the witness did not know the precise location of the ABiH multiple rocket launcher. He testified that he believes that the fire, the rocket fire came from the direction of a certain village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think he testified that he heard something about this weaponry being fired rather than seeing it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can draw your attention, our laptop is also I believe a few lines off --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give the words, we can search for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is the word Lokve, L-O-K-V-E and in ours it appears on page 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the evidence of the witness was they were firing approximately from the direction of the village of Lokve. So, a very general terms. Apart from that, your last question was rather confusing when you talked about the range. Because you asked the witness to compare the range with other weapons and then two weapons were in your question, and then, of course, the answer about the range is not quite clear. The witness may be brought into the courtroom again and I will put a few questions to him to start with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Gladly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, I have got a few intermediary questions for you. You talked about the multiple rocket launchers. Did you ever see them yourself, the multiple rocket launchers used by the other side in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw them myself, but I felt the consequences of these weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any specific knowledge of the technical details of these weapons? Did you ever see documentary -- documents on ranges, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would be the source of your knowledge of the range you just indicated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I served in the Yugoslav Army, and in the course of training you learn about all the weapons. There is a theoretical course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you were talking about the range of rocket launchers, were you referring to what you know about the weaponry used in the former Yugoslav Army, or were you referring to the range of these rocket launchers of which you heard they were of Chinese make?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I learned when I did my military service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... used in the former Yugoslav Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have -- do you know the precise position from where these rocket launchers were firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time when they fired at my crew with that multiple rocket launcher when they carried out a frontal attack of Hadzici, from direction of the village of Lokve. That's where the fire came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... from the direction of -- I take it then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lokve. Lokve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is more to the south as far as -- yes. So you know the direction, but not the precise position? Am I correct in understanding that you know the direction where they came from, but not the precise position from where they fired from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but not the precise position because if we had known the position, we would have used our artillery to fire at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to tell us about tanks. You told us about two tanks, there were two tanks present. Do you remember, the tanks from the opposing side, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you remind us where were these tanks active? Where were they firing from as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: From the Borak elevation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From that location precisely, and in direction of the town these tanks that I believe you said was a T-34 tank, although I don't have the transcript here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These tanks, what was their range, please, from that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Tanks and their charges --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that the witness has testified about this. It is accumulative and repetitive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least as far as the position is concerned, it is repetitive, Mr. Piletta-Zanin..

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Mr. President, but my only reason for this intervention is to make things very precise in relation to the questions that will follow with relation to the range, direction of the town. And I believe that my memory serves me correctly, because I have even quoted the type of the tank, the T-34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just -- yes, Mr. Mundis

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, again on our LiveNote page 53 line 25, and page 54, line 1, the witness talks about the range of the tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the question has been put to the witness, what was the range of that weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. But the question, Mr. President, now is as before, it is about the direction of the town. Now, bearing in mind the altitude, considering that we know that this was a -- from an elevation point, what were the areas in the city that were theoretically and practically could be hit. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis, when I look at page 52, line 21, 22, that was about a 20 millimetre anti-aircraft field gun, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, our LiveNote is slightly off, but it is page 53, line 25, and page 54, line 1, and the witness clearly testified as to the range of that weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give me some words that would enable me to find exactly the point you indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can do that, but I don't see any characteristic words without giving the actual numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I can read that. Page 54, line 5. It says: "The tank is a weapon that shoots, fires directly, I think up to 18 to 20.000 metres."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Mr. President, also the question is -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin attempted to rephrase it or explain it -- it was not the same question which he had originally put to the witness to which I objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the -- is there any dispute as to whether the distance from the points just indicated by the witness to area controlled by the Muslim forces, the BiH forces and the city would be not over 20 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There is no dispute about that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please move to your next subject, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke on several occasions about shellings, shellings carried out by the opposing army, about the BH Army, and you spoke to us about the type of the mortar, specifically about the 120-millimetre mortar. My question is the following: Did you personally see a number of craters that resulted from the shelling by 120-millimetre mortars, and did you see these craters in the asphalt; if you can answer with a yes or no, I would be very grateful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, hundreds of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you saw hundreds of these craters made by mortar shells of 120-millimetre calibre, can you tell us where as a general rule would the tail-fin of the shell be, and I am speaking about a hard surface, asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Well, not very far from where the shell would land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "not very far from where the shell would land" what do you mean by that? Can you give us an indication in terms of a distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: 20 or 30 metres, perhaps 50, depending on whether it would land between the buildings, and if it landed between the buildings, then it wouldn't have anywhere to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I conclude from your testimony that the tail-fin, as a general rule, is ejected from the what we call the crater; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... first putting the question in a wrong way and then repeat the question in a different way, that's not the way of examining witnesses. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did it ever happen to you that you found that tail-fin closer than that distance that you said was dozens of metres from the crater?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: There were cases that the tail-fin was embedded in the asphalt, that it was sticking out from the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, objection that was a mischaracterisation to the witness's testimony with respect to "dozens of metres."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 20 or 30, perhaps 50, I think that could create not great confusion. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to continue on another line of questioning in relation to weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were speaking about a field gun. Witness, did you see yourself other cannons or field guns apart from those that you've mentioned? I understand that you've also mentioned a Browning gun. Do you or have you seen any other field guns apart from those that you've already mentioned in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. You mean of the opposing side or in general?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking always about the opposing side, still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I first ask you, before you answer this question, did you see the Browning at the opposing side or with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see other types of heavy weapons, apart from those that you have mentioned so far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: I couldn't see the field guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you say that you were able to see tanks as such; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you know apart from the field guns that you've mentioned, other field guns that I do not wish to mention here, could have been used by the opposing side in the area that you knew, militarily speaking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, it is leading and leading calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's leading and yes. It is really calling for -- if you say "could have been used" that would ask -- "Do you know apart from the field guns that you mentioned, other field guns that could have been used," that is not a question about knowledge of the witness. So please rephrase or move to your next subject, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, is the Prosecution ready to re-examine the witness -- to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, Mr. DP18.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, unfortunately I will not be able to follow what Mr. Mundis is cross-examining, since I do not have the transcript and the LiveNote and to intervene, if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you can follow the cross-examination by carefully listening and I offer could you my assistance whenever you need to look back in the transcript. Please ask me and I will be glad to assist you. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis. Apart from that I inform you that by the end of the day you will get a full copy of the transcript of today so that you can use it later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I am also wondering if Mr. Piletta-Zanin could clarify whether or not he is receiving the LiveNote on the monitor in front of him which is distinct from the laptop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you see the text moving on your big screen? Mr. Piletta-Zanin nods in the affirmative. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified this morning that your company had a self propelled rocket, do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapon system was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: It is like a tank. It is on tracks and it has a gun which is 90-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it only have one -- this gun fired rockets, is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it only have the one gun for firing rockets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: No, not rockets, shells. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us it was a self-propelled rocket and now you are telling us that it didn't fire rockets, but shells, is that what you are telling us, witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I remember -- I can't give you the reference -- but I remember in the English transcript that there is -- it says self-propelled gun. This is what comes to my mind. Perhaps it can be checked, but I cannot do it, and you offered your assistance, and these are the three words that I still remember from the interpretation that I was listening to absent-mindedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, on our LiveNote it is at page 43, line 19, and the following question from Ms. Pilipovic repeated the phrase "self-propelled rocket."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I am first going to check what Mr. Mundis...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, you also sought clarification from the witness with respect to this system beginning on our system at page 44, line 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, could the English booth offer an explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please listen to the English booth, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness spoke of a "self-propelled", but in the B/C/S he didn't give a noun, which goes with it. Self-propelled gun, but there are different types of self-propelled weapons. It could be a vehicle, it could be any number of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that explains that, there might be some confusion as far as language is concerned, then now please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I wanted to say was that as far as I remember, what I read in the transcript as being the answer of the witness was in English, that he had said self-propelled gun. So I don't think that we should blame the witness if his words were translated as being self-propelled gun. I am almost certain of it. That's what I heard. I heard what the English booth had said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We only can follow though English. It is not my recollection that anyone blames the witness for anything at all. You asked whether we could assist you, I think we did it, and the interpreters explained how they translated the words and what difficulty they faced when translating the words of the witness. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just briefly I would like to respond to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. The witness did or the English translation does use the term "self-propelled gun" subsequently, however at the points which I indicated the words rocket does appear in the words of the transcript and I believe that was prior to Mr. Piletta-Zanin's entry into courtroom this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's not -- let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If the large coloured map could be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If no changes -- no, you need the map yourself, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could first draw your attention to Grivici, do you see that marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Grivici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If you could please look approximately 1 centimetre to the west and slightly north of the "G" in Grivici, do you see the numbers "712"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could perhaps the map could be zoomed in in that specific area where the witness is pointing at now, and perhaps have it centred so that -- a bit more to the right. Yes. If it could be zoomed in even more, that would be -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see where the numbers "712" appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those numbers refer to an elevation height; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could then please follow the red broken confrontation line to the -- as directly below the 712 where it proceeds eastward to the location Guncar, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately south of the words Guncar the numbers 806 appear on the map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is also a hill or small mountain at the elevation of 806 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you would then follow the broken red confrontation line in a south-easterly direction, do you see immediately north of the red line the numbers "828" below the word "Tinovo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Tinovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tinovo Brdo is a hill with an elevation of 828 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you look approximately 3 centimetres to the south-east of Tinovo Brdo, you will see the numbers "691" immediately to the north of Kasatici, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 691 would also refer to a hill at the elevation of 691 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continuing to the east of Kasatici, we see immediately below the word Lasac, another hill at 738 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes, this is Lasac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you were then to go in a north-easterly direction approximately 5 centimetres, you see Obeljak with an elevation of 1180 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, I thought you would just go over a few hills, but you are going for more. Since we are strictly bound to stop, since this courtroom has to be used at 2.15, one hill, I would allow you, but not more. If you have more, then please -- I know that it is very inconvenient to interrupt at this very moment, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is fine, Mr. President. If we need to break, we'll break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP18, I know that we have to stop just in the middle of a series of questions, but we will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom. You are ordered not to speak with anyone, whoever it is, not with counsel for the Prosecution, not with counsel for the Defence, not with anyone at all about your testimony you have been give asking you are about further to give. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning in this courtroom. We will adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
